titolo: Why the Congo Basin Is Still Off Limits to Humans
descrizione:
The Congo Basin covers more than three million square kilometers across six countries. It is the second largest rainforest on the planet, yet huge parts of it have never been surveyed by scientists, and some of the animals living there have only been recorded a handful of times.

In this documentary we explore what makes the deep Congo so hard to reach, from just how big the Congo Basin really is to the swamps and rivers that swallow roads and stop expeditions, disease, dangerous wildlife, animals hiding where no one can follow, and a canopy so thick that satellites can't see what's beneath it.

trascrizione_inizio: Say you decided to walk into the middle of the Congo Basin. Here is roughly how it goes. Hour one, your machete loses a fight to a plant. By hour three, the ground has already swallowed you to the waist and refuses to give your leg back. And after two days, your GPS is still searching for signal, the ants have found your camp, and something very large with tusks has noticed you. We have mapped the surface of Mars and even parked submarines on the floor of the deepest ocean trench. Yet, right in the middle of Africa, there is still a dark green hole in the map. And the forest itself is the reason it is there. The rule of this place is simple. The Congo does not keep people out with one wall. It stacks them one behind the other, and every time you climb over one, the next one is worse. Honestly, I would not make it to hour three. And most of my remaining time would be spent regretting my shoes. So, why can't you simply walk in? Why do boats and helicopters fail just as badly? What actually kills you first? And why might the best thing about this place be that we still cannot get inside? The first wall is made of plants. When most people hear the words impenetrable jungle, they picture the Amazon. Fair enough. The Amazon is enormous and brutal to explore.
